summary: Los Ratattuille: Asteroid Defense Mission is an action-packed Scratch video game created by elementary school students for the Space Mission Game challenge. Players pilot a spacecraft through an incoming asteroid field, using quick reflexes to dodge hazards or blast asteroids to earn points before an impact ends the mission, inspired by NASA's planetary defense and Near-Earth Object tracking efforts.
details:
What It Does:

Los Ratattuille: Asteroid Defense Mission is an interactive video game built in Scratch where players pilot a spaceship through a dangerous asteroid field. As asteroids fly straight toward the spacecraft, players must use quick reflexes to either steer out of the way or fire their ship's blasters to destroy incoming rocks. Every destroyed asteroid awards points, while failing to dodge or destroy an approaching asteroid results in a Game Over.

How It Works & How We Built It:

Our elementary school team (grades 2–4) programmed the entire game in Scratch using player-controlled movement, enemy trajectory loops, conditionals, and a live score variable. Each asteroid spawns and moves toward the player's ship, testing reaction speed and decision-making under pressure.

Why It Matters:

Navigating through deep space requires constant awareness of hazards like asteroids and space debris. Inspired by NASA's Near-Earth Object (NEO) tracking and planetary defense missions like DART, our game turns real space safety concepts into a fun, hands-on challenge that kids can play and learn from.

Tools & Resources Used:

- Scratch (MIT) for game logic, collision detection, controls, and scoring variables

- Custom spaceship, laser, and asteroid sprites

- Inspiration from NASA's Near-Earth Object (NEO) program and DART mission
